title: Verifier-Assisted versus LLM-Only Pre-deployment Network-Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre-deployment verifier with a bounded automated repair budget increases the fraction of intent-driven network-change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator. Each paired intent produced one shared_initial generation that was evaluated under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Outcomes: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single-shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We archive preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policies.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, configuration synthesis, and automated repair. For pre-deployment network changes, semantic correctness properties—sequencing constraints, reachability, and policy preservation—are operationally critical and cannot be assured by syntactic checks alone. A common engineering pattern is to pair a generative model with a deterministic validator and a bounded automated repair operator (generate→validate→repair) to reduce operational risk. How much deterministic rescue such guarded pipelines yield, however, depends on the experimental estimand (what is held fixed), the generator single-shot quality, the validator's semantic coverage, and the permitted repair budget.

We preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) to quantify the deterministic rescue achievable when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate using the declared generator (gpt-5-mini) and compared: (a) baseline — accept the single candidate without repair, and (b) guarded — run a deterministic validator and allow at most one automated repair which is then re-validated. The primary research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre-deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair?

Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a shared_initial estimand that conditions on a single LLM draw per intent; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the single automated repair transcript archived with the run; (3) an evidence-grounded interpretation of estimator conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work:
LLM applications for NetOps and intent translation have been documented across surveys and system papers that cover intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, automated test-case generation, and repair [1,2,3]. Tool-augmented, planner-centric and ReAct-style frameworks enable LLMs to call external validators and simulators to decompose multi-step NetOps workflows and coordinate tool outputs [2,4]. Empirical reports show that introducing deterministic checks and generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve surface correctness metrics relative to unconstrained generation, but effect sizes depend strongly on validator coverage, task distribution, and whether pipelines permit resampling or verifier-guided regeneration [3,5].

Two methodological themes motivate our choices. First, many prior evaluations conflate deterministic validation benefits with benefits from multiple independent model draws or verifier-guided regeneration; this conflation obscures the pure post-generation deterministic rescue attributable to validation alone [5]. Second, available NetOps benchmarks often emphasize syntactic or template correctness rather than semantically rich invariants (reachability, sequencing, policy preservation), limiting operational generality of evaluation claims and motivating verifier-centric evaluation artifacts [6,7,8]. Our study isolates the bounded post-hoc verifier/repair effect by conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent and by fixing a small automated repair budget.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the confirmatory design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) and fixed the primary estimand as the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier-pass proportion (guarded − baseline) on N = 300 paired intents after prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The analysis executor and multiplicity plan were fixed before observing main-run outcomes. The preregistration described an optional pilot (n = 60) for discordance estimation and power calibration; that pilot was not executed and no post-preregistration power recalculation was performed. We note this omission early because it reduced sensitivity to small absolute effects in the main run.

Task generation and stratification. Tasks were generated deterministically into a synthetic suite stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high). Each task manifest encodes the natural-language intent, initial and expected final states, ordered sequencing constraints (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), preserve_unspecified_state invariants, and protected_interfaces. Difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) determined stratum membership and ensured equal per-stratum sampling (100 pairs per stratum) in the confirmatory run.

Shared_initial protocol and model configuration. To isolate deterministic validator/repair rescue from generator resampling we implemented the shared_initial estimand: for each pair a single candidate was produced and reused for both baseline and guarded conditions. The declared generation model was gpt-5-mini. Reusing the identical candidate across conditions measures only deterministic validation and bounded repair applied to the same output and prevents differences due to additional model draws.

Deterministic validator and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic NetOps validator that checks sequencing invariants, required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability invariants encoded by the synthetic suite, and forbidden-template protections for protected interfaces. Scoring is binary: an unflagged candidate is a pass for the estimand. The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair attempt (repair budget ≤ 1). The repair operator is a constrained edit routine limited to localized sequencing and insertion edits (for example, inserting a missing 'admin down' before a VLAN/MTU change). Repair attempts are applied only to flagged candidates and are re-validated deterministically; repaired candidates that remain flagged count as failures for the guarded condition in the primary analysis.

Contamination controls and missingness rules. The preregistration included deterministic contamination detection and one intentionally broken negative control per complexity stratum. A pair would be excluded from confirmatory analysis only if both pipeline calls failed due to provider/infrastructure outage; if only one call failed the pair would be retained per the executor's policy and sensitivity analyses would treat single-call failures as failures where specified. All provider/API failures and exclusions are recorded; in this run no dual-call outages occurred and no pairs were excluded.

Execution instrumentation and auditing. The run used a hosted NetOps adapter under scientific_confirmatory execution. Key execution accounting values (planned episodes, completed episodes, complete pairs, model calls used, and stage counts) were recorded and archived to permit deterministic replay and to validate adherence to the shared_initial protocol and repair budget. Deterministic reconciliation verified pair and episode accounting consistency.
sections.results:
Execution integrity. The adapter completed the confirmatory run with completed_episode_count = 600, yielding complete_pair_count = 300 paired observations under the shared_initial protocol. Model call accounting recorded 301 model calls (300 shared_initial generations plus one repair invocation). Deterministic reconciliation confirmed consistent episode accounting and no provider/infrastructure failures or excluded pairs.

Primary outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test operating on discordant counts returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. Because discordance is minimal (m = n10 + n01 = 1), the exact test has limited sensitivity and the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point in this experimental context.

Per-stratum diagnostics. Per-stratum tallies were: low baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100 and guarded = 100/100. The single discordant example lies in the high stratum; low and medium strata were at ceiling under both conditions.

Repair diagnostic. The solitary discordant pair invoked the permitted automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial failure to a sequencing omission: the shared_initial candidate omitted an explicit 'admin down' step prior to a VLAN/MTU change required by the intent. The constrained repair performed a single localized insertion of the missing sequencing command; after this edit the deterministic validator reported valid == true. Thus the repair produced a deterministic rescue with one additional repair-stage call.

Contamination and missingness. Contamination checks reported no contamination flags. Missingness summary shows zero failed or unscorable episodes and zero excluded pairs under preregistered rules.

Operational cost. The guarded pipeline's deterministic rescue required a single additional repair-stage model call across 300 pairs, indicating minimal extra model-call cost in this run. The low empirical repair usage quantifies the guarded pipeline's small marginal model-call footprint under the chosen repair budget and edit operator.

Statistical interpretation. The confirmatory inferential outcome (p = 1.0) primarily reflects the paucity of discordant pairs under the shared_initial estimand and chosen synthetic suite. Exact McNemar inference depends only on n10 and n01; with n10 = 1 and n01 = 0 the two-sided exact p equals 1.0, indicating no statistically detectable difference under conventional two-sided testing. The paired bootstrap CI provides a complementary bound for effect size: the absolute paired improvement is plausibly between 0 and 0.01 given observed data and the preregistered estimand. These inferential statements apply strictly to the shared_initial conditioning (one LLM draw reused across conditions), the limited repair budget (≤1 constrained edit), the synthetic task distribution, and the declared generator and validator.
sections.discussion:
Estimand conditioning and operational alignment. Conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent reflects operational policies that constrain model calls for cost, latency, or governance reasons. Under such policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. Workflows that permit resampling, verifier-guided generation, or interactive steering change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates by exploiting generator variance; those workflows should be evaluated under a different preregistered design.

Ceiling effects and pilot omission. The preregistration targeted detection of a 10 percentage-point absolute improvement with planned power ≈0.8 based on a pilot to estimate discordance. Because the optional pilot was not executed, the main run confronted a near-ceiling baseline (299/300), producing minimal discordance (m = 1) and limited power to detect small absolute differences. This practical outcome highlights the value of small calibration pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling on chosen suites.

Validator coverage and failure-mode dependence. The observed single failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, forbidden ACL removal) were not observed at scale on this synthetic suite. The marginal utility of a guarded pipeline therefore depends on (a) the deployment distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness: richer validators that check reachability or ACL semantics may increase observed rescue rates.

Repair budget trade-offs. We intentionally limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to measure bounded deterministic rescue. Iterative repair, larger edit operators, or interactive verifier-guided generation would increase rescue opportunities but address a different estimand. The single repair trace archived with the run can inform design choices for permitted edit operators in production pipelines.

Implications for NetOps CI/CD. Organizations must align evaluation estimands with operational choices: if pipelines allow multiple model calls or verifier-guided regeneration, evaluations should allow resampling and interactive steering to measure achievable success rates under those policies. If model calls are tightly budgeted, the shared_initial estimand provides an operationally meaningful bound for deterministic verifier/repair rescue applied to a single candidate. Our artifact audit (model_calls_used = 301; repair_stage_count = 1) shows that in this run bounded repair produced measurable rescue at low additional model cost for the single rescued episode.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact-archived paired comparison between a verifier-assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single-shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini. Baseline single-shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). Deterministic validator+repair rescued one sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. The near-ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity to small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. We release full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility and targeted follow-up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, or repair budget.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real-world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and the declared deterministic validator were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single-shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre-specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post-preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
